removes.rationale: TD Cowen's dated reporting that Microsoft walked away from ~2GW of US/European data-center leases on AI-compute oversupply is the 'trim before crest' signal for the AI-capex sub-thesis, so MSFT gives way to fresh European-rearmament exposure while NVDA (the more direct AI-compute bet, recovered from the DeepSeek scare) is retained.

news_evidence.summary: TD Cowen: Microsoft walked away from ~200MW-2GW of data center developments and leases

rationale_overall: One paired swap at the size-2 cap: MSFT exits on a dated MSFT-specific AI-capex pullback (TD Cowen's abandoned data-center leases, Feb 24 and Mar 26), exactly the 'trim before crest' behavior the profile asks for even while the AI wave itself hasn't crested. NVDA is kept as the more direct AI-compute exposure (the Jan 27 DeepSeek -17% selloff faded quickly). RTX enters as the first non-AI slot, riding the concrete buildup of European defense/rearmament (EU EUR800B Readiness 2030, Germany debt-brake reform) with a record $218B backlog as an earnings anchor. Result: NVDA, RTX.
